    A Ghost in Your Ear

    7:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Most days

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

    Curtis Stigers

    7:00 PM · Birdland Theater, Hell's Kitchen · $35.46

    For the past 30 years, the singer, songwriter, saxophonist and guitarist Curtis Stigers has been making records that confound those who try to categorize his music or put him in a box. Stigers burst onto the recording scene in 1991 with his eponymously-titled debut album, which sold 1.5 million copies and spawned several self-penned, pop/soul hit singles, including , "rdquo" -> You're All That Matters To Me", , "rdquo" -> Never Saw A Miracle" and the worldwide top-ten hit, , "rdquo" -> I Wonder Why." The next year the singer/songwriter/saxophonist recorded Nick Lowe's , "rdquo" -> (What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace Love and Understanding" for , "rdquo" -> The Bodyguard" soundtrack, which has sold over 45 million copies worldwide. Stigers recorded two more pop-oriented albums in the 1990s and made guest appearances on several albums, including two by his early musical mentor, the legendary jazz pianist Gene Harris. In 2001 Stigers pivoted artistically and signed with Concord Jazz. Over the next 18 years he recorded nine genre-busting albums, combining his jazz sensibilities with his love for emotional, well-written modern songs from a wide variety of sources including rock, blues, soul, country and folk. During this period Stigers co-wrote and sang , "rdquo" -> This Life", the Emmy Award-nominated theme song to the wildly popular TV show , "rdquo" -> Sons Of Anarchy", and also made cameo appearances in the Seth MacFarlane movies , "rdquo" -> Ted" and , "rdquo" -> Ted 2". All the while, Stigers was cultivating a successful and enduring touring career, playing concerts around the world, performing songs from his jazz albums as well as newly reconstructed , "rdquo" -> jazz" versions of his hit songs from his early pop albums.

Beginning his career in the 1960s with Jaki Byard and Eric Dolphy, Cannonball Adderley, and a five year stint with the Miles Davis Quintet, Ron also performed and recorded with notables including Bill Evans, B.B. King, and Dexter Gordon. Ron Carters various ensembles, big band to trio, feature a whos who of the finest players on the NYC scene with, an absolute commitment to musical sublimity [that] exudes refined elegance and sonic power.
